name: Luspatercept
drug_class: Erythroid maturation agent (activin receptor type IIB ligand trap)

discovery.note: A fusion of the modified extracellular domain of activin receptor type IIB with human IgG1 Fc, which traps TGF-beta superfamily ligands that inhibit late-stage erythropoiesis.

tagline: Ligand trap that corrects ineffective red cell maturation in thalassaemia and MDS
summary: Luspatercept is a recombinant fusion protein that binds selected TGF-beta superfamily ligands such as GDF11, reducing SMAD2/3 signalling that blocks late red cell maturation. It reduces transfusion needs in beta-thalassaemia and lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes.
mechanism: In ineffective erythropoiesis, excess signalling by TGF-beta superfamily ligands through activin receptors and SMAD2/3 holds erythroid precursors at late stages, so many die in the marrow.

Luspatercept acts as a decoy receptor, sequestering ligands such as GDF11, GDF8 and activin B. This releases the block and promotes maturation of late-stage erythroblasts, increasing haemoglobin independently of erythropoietin.
uses: Anaemia in lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes, including first-line in ESA-naive patients

history.title: Celgene partnership
history.detail: Acceleron and Celgene begin collaborating on activin receptor ligand traps.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved for transfusion-dependent beta-thalassaemia after the BELIEVE trial.

history.title: MDS approval
history.detail: FDA approves use in lower-risk MDS with ring sideroblasts after MEDALIST; EU approval follows.

history.title: Merck buys Acceleron
history.detail: Merck acquires Acceleron; Bristol Myers Squibb (which had acquired Celgene) retains luspatercept.

history.title: First-line MDS
history.detail: COMMANDS trial leads to FDA approval before ESAs in lower-risk MDS.

facts: The FDA first approved luspatercept in November 2019 for anaemia in transfusion-dependent beta-thalassaemia; anaemia in lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes followed in April 2020.
Bristol Myers Squibb acquired the originator, Acceleron Pharma, in 2021 for about $11.5 billion.
